## Why
- **R1** — query-string API keys leak into logs and proxies (CWE-598); a security fix built by an outside agent needs an Opus review before it ships. Serves platform hygiene/security.
- **R2** — model-eval measurement feeds every orchestration cost/quality decision; it is built and idle in draft.
- **R3** — the providers landing demo form is the B2B top of funnel; a client/server email-check mismatch drops demo requests.
- **C1** — a docs-only chore with zero real check runs stalls silently.
- **B1** — critical path to the Nova showpiece demo (weekly priority 1): every later seed slice needs a safe, repeatable reseed. Stephen chose to clear reviews first.

## How
- Lanes: R1/R2 start now in two local slots; R3 takes the third. B1 starts when a slot frees (reviews own their PR to merge, so the first merge frees it). Assumption: if a review is parked waiting on Stephen for over an hour, B1 still waits for a free slot (no fourth slot during the day).
- Review routing cross-vendor: Cursor/GPT → Claude Opus; Claude-built → Codex Sol.
- PR branches are checked out in other sessions' idle worktrees; reviewers use their own worktree on a `review/<branch>` local branch and push with an explicit refspec to the PR branch.

The store is the live layer between those two: seeded from the published plan on approval, carrying every mid-day transition and steer, with a subscription/event stream for real-time monitoring and dynamic changes.

Why: Stephen wants a durable, phone-friendly fleet view; the pi UI's attention-first layout is the best existing design.
